metaTitle: Electrical Contractors in Ontario: A Buyer's Guide
metaDescription: What to know before hiring an electrician in Ontario, including ESA licensing and permits, panel upgrades, EV chargers, costs and red flags to avoid.
intro: Electrical work in Ontario homes must meet Electrical Safety Authority requirements, and most jobs need a permit pulled by a licensed electrical contractor. Panel upgrades, rewiring and EV charger installs all carry real safety stakes if done by unlicensed labour.
whatToLookFor: A Licensed Electrical Contractor registered with the ESA
An ESA permit pulled and inspection scheduled for the scope of work
Experience with your specific job type, such as panel upgrades or EV chargers
Clear labelling and documentation of any panel or circuit changes
Written confirmation of what inspection and sign-off will look like
typicalCostNotes: Electrical costs range widely by scope, a simple outlet or fixture swap costs far less than a full panel upgrade or a whole-home rewire, and older homes with knob-and-tube or aluminum wiring often add cost once walls are opened. EV charger installs depend heavily on how far the panel is from the parking spot and whether the panel has capacity, and trenching for an underground run can add meaningfully to the total. Confirm whether the ESA permit fee is included in the quote.
questionsToAsk: Are you a Licensed Electrical Contractor registered with the ESA?
Will an ESA permit be pulled for this work?
Does our panel have capacity for this, or does it need upgrading?
What happens if you find knob-and-tube or aluminum wiring?
Who schedules the ESA inspection, and when does that happen?
redFlags: No ESA licence number provided when asked
Willingness to skip the permit for a discounted cash price
No mention of an inspection after the work is done
